candidates.attacker_control: The attacker is any authenticated user (e.g. ROLE_USER). The only input needed is a document/informatieobject UUID (path variable `documentId` / `documentId`) plus the plugin configuration id, which the same unprotectd endpoints hand out. Document UUIDs can be enumerated without guessing via the authenticated process-instance search API, which returns process rows including `BUSINESS_KEY_` (= case document UUID) and all process variables (see camunda-process-instance-v2.xml select `searchInstances`, ProcessInstance DTO, and ProcessHttpSecurityConfigurer lines 59-61), so a case the attacker may not view still yields the identifier needed for steps below.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked whether the services enforce PBAC implicitly: JsonSchemaDocumentService.get/findBy do require VIEW, and DocumentenApiVersionService.getVersionByDocumentId (used by the v2 zaken-api endpoint) calls that method, so the v2 path is guarded; the v1 path and the plugin-level download/modify/delete do not call it. Checked the `authorizationEnabled` flag (valtimo.authorization.zgwDocuments.enabled, default false, true in the sample app): it only adds global ResourcePermission VIEW/VIEW_LIST/MODIFY/DELETE checks in DocumentenApiClient/ZakenApiClient, not case/document-scoped checks, and it is absent from the zaken-api ZaakDocumentService path. Checked that the endpoints are reachable: ZakenApiHttpSecurityConfigurer and DocumentenApiHttpSecurityConfigurer limit them to .authenticated(); default-deny applies only to unmatched paths. Checked that the resource/plugin beans are registered (ZakenApiAutoConfiguration.zaakDocumentService/ZaakDocumentResource, DocumentenApiAutoConfiguration). No test sources exist in the snapshot to confirm expected behavior, and the Documenten API might theoretically restrict the configured service account, which cannot be verified from this source tree.
candidates.impact: Cross-case confidentiality and integrity breach: any authenticated user who obtains document identifiers can read zaak metadata and file metadata (names, authors, titles, confidentiality classification) for cases they cannot access, download the underlying document content from the Documenten API, and (with the default flag) modify or delete those documents. This bypasses the platform's central PBAC model, which in the sample configuration restricts ROLE_USER document VIEW to assigned/leningen cases (app/gzac/config/pbac/document.permission.json). There is no evidence the external Documenten API re-checks the end user because the backend uses its own plugin credentials (client-credentials authentication).
candidates.prerequisites: Authenticated session. A Zaken API plugin configuration must exist for the case (normal for ZGW deployments) and the Documenten API plugin must be configured for download/modify/delete. `valtimo.authorization.zgwDocuments.enabled` must be left at its default false for the documenten-api operations to run with no permission at all; even when true, the check is a global `ResourcePermission` (view/modify/delete) rather than a per-document case-authorization check. No special role beyond authentication is required for the zaken-api v1 endpoints.
candidates.root_cause: The ZGW-facing endpoints authenticate the caller but never require Valtimo's document-level PBAC permission (VIEW/MODIFY/DELETE on JsonSchemaDocument / related file) for the documentId or informatieobject they operate on. `ZaakInstanceLinkService.getByDocumentId` looks the zaak link up directly from the repository, `ZaakDocumentService.getInformatieObjectenAsRelatedFiles`/`getZaakByDocumentId` build on it without any authorization call, and `DocumentenApiService.downloadInformatieObject`/`getInformatieObject`/`modifyInformatieObject`/`deleteInformatieObject` only delegate to the plugin (whose client checks are a global `ResourcePermission` gated by `valtimo.authorization.zgwDocuments.enabled`, default false, never scoped to the document). By contrast, `JsonSchemaDocumentService.getDocumentBy`/`get` (and the v2 zaken-api endpoint through `DocumentenApiVersionService.getVersionByDocumentId`) do call `authorizationService.requirePermission(..., VIEW, document)`, showing the intended control.
candidates.title: Missing document-level authorization on ZGW zaak/document endpoints (cross-case document access)
candidates.trace: 1) Attacker lists process definitions (GET /api/v1/process/definition, authenticated) and calls POST /api/v2/process/{processDefinitionName}/search or /api/v1/process/{processDefinitionName}/search; the MyBatis query `searchInstances` returns BUSINESS_KEY_ plus all historical variables with no PBAC filter, leaking case document UUIDs. 2) GET /api/v1/zaken-api/document/{documentId}/files (or /zaak) -> ZaakDocumentService.getInformatieObjectenAsRelatedFiles -> DefaultZaakUrlProvider.getZaakUrl -> ZaakInstanceLinkService.getByDocumentId (repository lookup, no authorization) -> ZakenApiPlugin.getZaakInformatieObjecten -> returns RelatedFileDto entries containing fileId (informatieobject UUID), pluginConfigurationId, bestandsnaam, auteur, titel, vertrouwelijkheidaanduiding and, for /zaak, the full ZaakResponse. 3) GET /api/v1/documenten-api/{pluginConfigurationId}/files/{fileId}/download -> DocumentenApiService.downloadInformatieObject -> DocumentenApiPlugin -> DocumentenApiClient.downloadInformatieObjectContent; only the optional global flag check runs, so the file content is returned. 4) With the same identifiers, PUT (modify) or DELETE on /api/v1/documenten-api/{pluginConfigurationId}/files/{fileId} alter/remove the informatieobject. In all steps the caller never needs any permission on the JsonSchemaDocument that owns the zaak/document. The v2 endpoint (/api/v2/zaken-api/document/{documentId}/files) shows the intended behavior because DocumentenApiVersionService.getVersionByDocumentId calls documentService.get(documentId), which requires VIEW on the document.
candidates.unverified: No runtime or integration verification was performed. The exact exploitability depends on the deployment (which ZGW plugins are configured, whether `valtimo.authorization.zgwDocuments.enabled` is true, and whether the external Documenten/Zaken APIs apply additional authorization for the backend's service credentials). The claim that document UUIDs are obtainable in practice relies on the unrestricted process-instance search endpoints, which is itself a separate unconfirmed lead (see rejected leads).
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-862 Missing Authorization (PBAC bypass for case documents)

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned source tree (3,089 files) via source scope, file listing, text search and targeted reading. Focus areas: PBAC/authorization service and specifications; document, case, case_, document-snapshot and dashboard services; form/form-flow/form-view-model; process/process-document/task core resources and security configurers; resource/temporary-resource-storage; objects-api and zgw modules (zaken-api, documenten-api, notificaties-api, objecten-api, catalogi-api, object-management, portaaltaak, verzoek); connector/plugin/importer/exporter. No tests exist in the snapshot, so no test-based confirmation was possible. Binary-like files, files over 5 MiB and symlinks: none excluded per get_source_scope (0 of each). Coverage is broad but not exhaustive at line level for all 3,089 files.
limitations: No execution, tests, scanners or runtime verification were allowed/performed; all conclusions are static source reasoning.
The snapshot contains no test sources, so intended authorization behavior could not be cross-checked with tests.

The candidate depends on deployment configuration not fully visible here (which ZGW plugins are configured, whether `valtimo.authorization.zgwDocuments.enabled` is enabled, and whether the external Documenten/Zaken APIs apply their own authorization to the backend service credentials).

UUID-based access control is a central uncertainty: the zaken-api/documenten-api weakness becomes trivially exploitable only when document UUIDs leak (e.g. via the process-instance search endpoints, itself an unconfirmed lead); otherwise it requires knowledge of an identifier.

Some modules were skimmed rather than exhaustively read (mail, keycloak-iam, exact-plugin, haalcentraal, contactmoment, klant, besluit, openzaak legacy, outbox, changelog, localization, value-resolver); other vulnerabilities may exist there.
Line references are from the current snapshot and may be affected by later/earlier revisions in the benchmark corpus.

rejected_leads.lead: Process instance search exposes all process instances and variables to any authenticated user (POST /api/v1|v2/process/{processDefinitionName}/search is only `.authenticated()` in ProcessHttpSecurityConfigurer lines 59-61; ProcessResource lines 501-530; MyBatis camunda-process-instance-v2.xml lines 44-73 returns BUSINESS_KEY_ and all ACT_HI_VARINST rows with no authorization filter; ProcessInstance DTO lines 23-31 exposes businessKey and variables). It is a credible missing-authorization issue (and an identifier source for the candidate) but I could not confirm that this endpoint is intended to be admin-only, so it was not submitted as the candidate.
rejected_leads.reason: Unconfirmed intent/severity: no per-process-instance PBAC model exists in the codebase, and the endpoint may be considered non-sensitive process metadata by the project.

rejected_leads.lead: PUT /api/v1/process/definition/{processDefinitionId}/xml/timer is `.authenticated()` (ProcessHttpSecurityConfigurer line 38) while the neighbouring deployment endpoint requires ADMIN (line 64), and it deploys a new process definition via ProcessShortTimerService (ProcessResource lines 609-618; ProcessShortTimerService lines 56-59/144-148). ProcessShortTimerService also parses XML with an unhardened DocumentBuilderFactory (lines 75-88, no external-entity restriction).
rejected_leads.reason: The deployed content is derived from an already-deployed process model and the impact is mostly limited to definition clutter/DoS; the XXE variant needs a malicious BPMN to already be in the repository (deployment itself requires ADMIN). Impact and attacker control are weaker than the selected candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: QueryCondition evaluates a SpEL expression with a plain StandardEvaluationContext when the dashboard/widget queryValue contains 'localDateTimeNow' (contract/.../QueryCondition.kt lines 88-117), which could allow expression injection; DocumentMigrationService and FormFlow SpelExpressionProcessor are similar.
rejected_leads.reason: All reachable configuration entry points (dashboard/widget/form-flow management APIs) require ADMIN, and no non-admin path to set the expression string was found, so no low-privilege exploit could be established.

rejected_leads.lead: Temporary resource upload metadata can set an arbitrary `documentId`, and ResourceUploadedToDocumentEventListener/UploadProcessService start a process for that case with runWithoutAuthorization (resource/temporary-resource-storage .../TemporaryResourceStorageResource.kt lines 46-67; zgw/zaken-api .../uploadprocess/ResourceUploadedToDocumentEventListener.kt lines 36-57; UploadProcessService lines 37-59).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires a case UUID and an upload process configured for the victim case definition, and the case-level check is only omitted when `valtimo.authorization.zgwDocuments.enabled` is false; same UUID-knowledge caveat as the candidate, but narrower impact (attacker-added file).

rejected_leads.lead: POST /api/v1/permissions calls Class.forName(resource) on user-supplied class names (authorization/.../PermissionResource.kt lines 45-81, PermissionAvailableRequest.kt lines 26-29), reachable by any authenticated user (ValtimoAuthorizationHttpSecurityConfigurer line 40).
rejected_leads.reason: Class loading alone is not demonstrably exploitable without a suitable gadget static initializer, and the endpoint returns only booleans.

summary: Reviewed the Valtimo backend snapshot (3,089 files, Java/Kotlin/Spring). I traced attacker-reachable data paths around the document/case PBAC model and the ZGW (zaken-api/documenten-api) modules. Strongest candidate: the ZGW document endpoints apply only authentication (plus an optional, global resource-permission flag) and never enforce the per-document PBAC check that the document module itself enforces, so any authenticated user who knows/derives a document UUID can read zaak and document metadata and download/modify/delete Documenten API documents for cases they cannot view. Evidence includes the unprotected v1 zaken-api endpoints, the documenten-api download/modify/delete endpoints, and the contrast with the v2 endpoint that indirectly requires JsonSchemaDocument VIEW. No runtime verification was performed; findings are source-based leads only.
